title: PUT /api/organizations/me merges settings.* by dot-notation so Overview and Settings tab saves don't clobber each other
description: updateMyOrg (organization.controller.js:20-63) applies req.body.settings key-by-key rather than replacing the whole settings object, so a save from OrganizationOverviewTab (industry, orgSize) does not wipe out fields previously saved by SettingsTab (timezone, dateFormat) in the same session.
preconditions: org.settings already has timezone='America/New_York' and dateFormat='MM/DD/YYYY' from a prior Settings tab save
steps: Call PUT /api/organizations/me with body { settings: { industry: 'Financial Services', orgSize: '51-100' } }
Call GET /api/organizations/me and inspect the full settings object
expectedResult: settings.industry and settings.orgSize are updated to the new values while settings.timezone and settings.dateFormat remain unchanged from the earlier save.

title: PUT /api/organizations/me accepts arbitrary unlisted keys under settings with no server-side allow-list
description: org.settings is Mixed with no schema validation (organization.model.js:68-101), and updateMyOrg applies whatever keys are present in req.body.settings. There is no allow-list restricting which settings.* keys are legal, so a caller with only organization.update can persist keys the UI never exposes.
preconditions: Logged in as org admin with organization.update permission
steps: Call PUT /api/organizations/me with body { settings: { arbitraryUnknownKey: 'anything', settings: { nested: true } } }
Call GET /api/organizations/me and inspect settings
expectedResult: Current behavior: the unrecognized key is persisted verbatim and returned on read — this is a schema-validation gap (Mixed type + no allow-list) that should be flagged for remediation rather than treated as a pass/fail regression of intended behavior.

title: Invite duplicate-email guard returns the correct 409 variant for same-org-invited, same-org-active, and cross-org cases
description: user.controller.js create() (lines 316-511) runs a global User.findOne({email}) lookup (not scoped to the target org) and branches into three distinct 409 messages depending on the existing record's org and status.
preconditions: user1@acme.com exists in Org A with status='invited'
user2@acme.com exists in Org A with status='active'
user3@acme.com exists in Org B with status='active'
steps: POST /api/users with email=user1@acme.com against Org A
POST /api/users with email=user2@acme.com against Org A
POST /api/users with email=user3@acme.com against Org A
expectedResult: Step 1: 409 'An invitation has already been sent... use Resend Invite'. Step 2: 409 'A user with this email already exists'. Step 3: 409 '...already registered under a different organisation.' No new User document is created in any case.

title: Inviting a user beyond the plan's seat limit returns 402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED with resource/current/limit details
description: quota.consume(orgId,'users',1) throws QuotaExceededError which billing/errors.js maps to HTTP 402 with errorCode='QUOTA_EXCEEDED' and details={resource,current,limit}. Applies only when isPricingV1Enabled(orgId) and billingMode!=='project'.
preconditions: Org on pricing v1, billingMode='organization', plan seat limit=10, usage.users=10
steps: POST /api/users with a new valid invite payload for this org
expectedResult: Response is 402 with body { success:false, errorCode:'QUOTA_EXCEEDED', details:{ resource:'users', current:10, limit:10 } }. No User document or Keycloak invite is created.

title: Resend Invite is rejected with 409 once the user has an associated keycloakUserId
description: resendInvite (user.controller.js:738-781) only proceeds if status==='invited' && !keycloakUserId. Once a user has accepted (or was ever bound to a KC identity via the fallback direct-create path), resend must be blocked rather than silently re-sending or erroring generically.
preconditions: A user record with status='invited' but keycloakUserId already set (e.g. via the emailFailed fallback path)
steps: Call POST /api/users/:id/resend-invite for this user
expectedResult: 409 Conflict 'This user has already activated their account.' — no duplicate Keycloak invite email is sent.

title: Soft-removing a user leaves their ProjectMember rows intact; only permanentRemove cleans them up
description: remove() (user.controller.js:599-646) sets isActive=false, status='removed', releases seat quota, and disables (not deletes) the Keycloak account, but performs no ProjectMember cleanup. Only permanentRemove (DELETE /:id/permanent, line 658) calls ProjectMember.deleteMany({userId}).
preconditions: A user is an active ProjectMember on Project X
steps: Call DELETE /api/users/:id (soft remove) for this user
Query ProjectMember records for this userId
Then call DELETE /api/users/:id/permanent for the same user
Query ProjectMember records again
expectedResult: After the soft remove, the ProjectMember row for Project X still exists referencing the now-removed user (current gap — the user may still surface in project team listings depending on downstream isActive filtering). After permanentRemove, the ProjectMember row is deleted.

title: Deleting a custom role that is still assigned to a user does not cascade or warn — the user silently loses role-derived permissions
description: role.remove (role.controller.js:220-255) has no userCount>0 guard before deletion. Users whose roleIds still reference the deleted Role document lose those role permissions the next time the permission cache is invalidated, with no error surfaced anywhere.
preconditions: User Bob has roleIds=['<auditor-role-id>'] and no extraPermissions
steps: As org admin, DELETE /api/roles/:id for the 'Auditor' role while Bob still holds it
As Bob, attempt GET /api/evidence (requires evidence.read)
expectedResult: Current behavior: the DELETE succeeds with no warning about assigned users. Bob's subsequent request is denied (403) once his permission cache refreshes, because the deleted role no longer resolves to any permissions — this silent-loss gap should be flagged for remediation (e.g. block delete while userCount>0, or reassign a fallback role).

title: Billing calls for a project-billed organization require an explicit projectId or return 400
description: billingProjectAccess middleware (billing.routes.js:56-67) enforces that project-billed orgs (billingMode='project') supply a projectId on GET /v1/billing/plan, /usage, /ai-credits; only billing.admin holders may act across projects they are not a member of.
preconditions: Caller holds only billing.read (project member, not billing.admin)
steps: Call GET /api/v1/billing/usage with no projectId query param
Call GET /api/v1/billing/usage?projectId=<a project the caller is not a member of>
expectedResult: Step 1: 400 Bad Request 'projectId is required for project-billed organizations.' Step 2: request is rejected (caller lacks billing.admin so cross-project access without membership is denied).

title: Keycloak profile update failure during a user edit is swallowed — Mongo update succeeds and returns 200 while Keycloak silently drifts out of sync
description: user.controller.js:575-589 calls updateKeycloakUserProfile/setUserEnabled with a fire-and-forget .catch(()=>{}) after the Mongo document is already saved. A Keycloak outage or error during this call is never surfaced to the caller and never retried.
preconditions: Keycloak admin API mocked/stubbed to reject on updateUserProfile for this test run
steps: As org admin, PUT /api/users/:id with a changed firstName/lastName while the Keycloak call is forced to fail
Inspect the HTTP response
Separately query the Keycloak user record for the same user
expectedResult: Current behavior: the API returns 200 with the Mongo record updated, with no error field indicating the Keycloak sync failure. The Keycloak record remains stale (unsynced name) — a real gap worth alerting/retry logic for.
